title: Week-of-launch playbook: throttle windows, dependency map, and rollback triggers
creator: Amelia Chen
description: Objective: Create an actionable, week-of-launch playbook that coordinates throttling windows, dependency-aware rollout sequences, and explicit rollback triggers across Runtime, Console, and API surfaces. Scope: 1) Define per-region throttle windows and traffic ramp plans; 2) Produce a dependency matrix tying feature flags, infra changes, and third-party providers to launch gates; 3) Specify concrete rollback conditions, automated triggers, and manual escalation paths; 4) Wire monitoring dashboards and post-launch validation checks. Stakeholders: Product, Runtime Eng, Console Eng, API Platform, SRE, Sales Engineering. Deliverables: 1) Week-of-launch timeline (hour-by-hour for cutover day), 2) Dependency map with owners and mitigation steps, 3) Throttle and burst policies per route and region, 4) Runbook with rollback triggers + escalation matrix, 5) Preflight checklist and a single-pane launch dashboard link. Acceptance criteria: - Playbook reviewed and signed by Runtime, Console, API leads - Throttle policies validated against canary traffic test and backed out plan exists - Monitoring alerts and dashboards linked in runbook - Post-launch postmortem template included and assigned owners
comments: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Console, API, and SRE. Captured initial risks: regional capacity variability, legacy feature flags with unclear owners, and data plane schema change scheduled same week.

2026-03-02: Drafted hour-by-hour timeline for cutover day. Decision: prefer 3-tier ramp (10%, 40%, 100%) with 30-60 minute observation windows between steps. Assigned Rafael to validate runtime autoscaler behavior during 40% ramp.

2026-03-03: Identified two feature flags without clear owners; PM to assign and create follow-ups. Added emergency rollback trigger: sustained 30% increase in 95th p50 response latency for >10 minutes across any region.
2026-03-04: SRE proposed adding low-cost secondary fallback model for hosted inference routes as a graceful degradation path. Action: Eng to prototype and measure quality delta by 2026-03-12.

2026-03-05: Wired prototype Launch Dashboard (Grafana) for cutover metrics: token/sec, p95 latency, error budget burn, queue length, and infra GPU utilization. Link added to runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/launch-playbooks/week-of-launch-dashboard
2026-03-06: Legal asked for audit log check for private deployments during rollout. Added a preflight verification item: confirm audit-log ingestion for affected customers is not interrupted.

2026-03-07: Cross-team review: Console requested a shorter observation window for UI-facing features (15 minutes) to reduce end-user exposure. Compromise accepted for Console-only routes with additional canary traffic tagging.

2026-03-08: PM review complete. Next steps: finalize dependency matrix (owners assigned), lock throttle policies, and run a dry-run on 2026-03-15 against staging. Rafael to open tickets for rollback automation and dashboard finalization.
